stage: Batch process phase, integer: 1 = initial heating, 5 = active phase (valve open), 8 = cooldown/end of batch. Not a physical measurement, a state.
valve_open: Binary state (0/1) of the dosing valve: open or closed. Doesn't indicate how much current/voltage it's drawing, only the logical state — to check for an electrical fault look at valve_current/valve_voltage, not this field.
valve_current: Electrical current measured on the dosing valve's coil, in Amperes. During a normal opening (phase 5) it typically stays between 0.8 and 1.0A. A value well above that range (e.g. >1.5A) during ANY phase, especially with the valve closed or during cooldown (phase 8), indicates a possible electrical/mechanical valve fault, not a normal condition.
valve_voltage: Voltage across the valve's coil, in Volts. Normal during opening: 4.6-4.8V. Abnormal values carry the same meaning as valve_current.
flow_sensor: Flow sensor reading, dimensionless in this sample dataset — always 0 in the sample data, not meaningful for this batch.
heater_on: Binary state (0/1) of the heater: on during phase 1 (initial heating), off in other phases. Expected behavior, not an anomaly.
heater_current: Current drawn by the heater, in Amperes — always 0 in the sample data (the heater in this dataset has no active dedicated current sensor).
power_density: Process power density, arbitrary unit. Around 11 during the active phases (1 and 5), drops to 0 during cooldown (phase 8) — expected behavior.
pump_a: Binary state (0/1) of the primary pump: active during phases 1 and 5, off during cooldown (phase 8) — expected behavior.
pump_b: Binary state (0/1) of the secondary pump: always active in this dataset, regardless of phase — expected behavior, not an anomaly.
temperature: Process temperature, in Celsius. Near zero during phase 1, rises to 90-200°C during the active phase (5), returns near zero during cooldown (phase 8). An elevated value (>10°C) during phase 8, outside expected behavior, can indicate a problem.
concentration: Product concentration, arbitrary unit — always 0 in the sample data, not meaningful for this batch.
efficiency: Process efficiency, dimensionless (0-1) — always 0 in the sample data, not meaningful for this batch (the real yield indicator here is yield_score in the batch's record, not this telemetry metric).
